name: preferences-evolve
$comment: Capture → reinforce → promote → supersede → decay/retire. Feedback comments go through the offline heuristic (no scripted proposal needed); the contradiction is scripted so the exact slot/value is under test.

steps.note: A plain coding question. Nothing preference-shaped, so the triage gate keeps the extractor out.

turn.user: How do I fix this TypeScript error: Property 'foo' does not exist on type 'Bar'?
turn.assistant: Here is a long, exhaustive explanation of structural typing...

steps.note: Explicit feedback on that answer: two preferences in one comment (format.length=short, format.lists=bullets).
The same preference restated later: same slot + same value on the same node → reinforce, not a second hint.

turn.user: Explain what a closure is in JavaScript.

feedback.text: again, keep it shorter please, bullet points work best

steps.note: A consolidation pass promotes a reinforced hint from captured to consolidated (explicit half-life 90 d → 180 d).
Contradiction: the user now wants detail. Scripted proposal on the same slot (format.length) with a new value → the old hint is superseded.

turn.user: Walk me through how the V8 garbage collector works.

ops.text: Prefers detailed explanations with the reasoning shown.
ops.rationale: the user corrected the short-answer preference

steps.note: An inferred hint from a plain turn (no feedback): 'i usually' trips the triage gate and the offline heuristic reads 'in Python' → code.language=python, source inferred, half-life 30 d.

turn.user: I usually write in Python — can you show me how to memoize this function?

steps.note: 45 days later the inferred hint has decayed to ~0.35 of its weight — visible, but still above the 0.15 retirement floor.
Another 45 days (90 total): inferred/captured weight ≈ 0.125 < 0.15 → retired (decayed). The explicit hints, with 90 d and 180 d half-lives, survive.
Recall renders what survived: detail + bullets, never the superseded short-answer hint.

recall.text: How does async/await work in TypeScript code under the hood?
